title: Week 5
coldOpen:
Jeff has officially made ignoring him irresponsible; Mike went 4-0, won by 87, and somehow left the week with a complaint; Max won his Super Bowl and half the league celebrated with him; Tanish panic-bought a quarterback, then watched the guy he was worried about beat Buffalo; and Greg is four games into my championship pick and already holding a liquidation sale.

Welcome to the Week 4 PDL Power Rankings.

1: I have bad news for everyone who has enjoyed this section for the last three weeks.
Delco was actually decent this week.
No beating Joe while scoring 124. No Tyler Shough sitting on my bench making me reconsider the current QB situation I have. No spending 400 words investigating why Mitsubishi Marv wasn't involved.
I just beat Welch by 40 points.
This sucks. I don't know how to write this.
The obvious place to start is Kyren Williams, which means approximately 85% of the PDL can avert their eyes.
Kyren had 16 carries for 80 yards and two touchdowns against the Eagles. He also caught 10 passes on 13 targets for another 67 yards.
31.7 PDL points.
The Philadelphia Eagles had 172 total yards of offense.
Kyren Williams had 147.

So while I was watching my actual football team go 0-for-12 on third down and slowly die in front of me, the running back carrying my fantasy team was responsible for nearly as much offense by himself.
So even when I should be happy, I am destroyed.

I have never understood why this league hates Kyren so much. Every offseason we apparently hold a meeting where everyone agrees that this is finally the year Sean McVay realizes he doesn't like him. Blake Corum is coming. He's too slow. He's not explosive enough. The Rams will draft somebody.
McVay's response this week was to give him 26 touches and throw at him 13 times.
Thirteen targets.
I am deliberately not checking how long it would take Arizona to give Marv 13 targets because I'm trying to have one nice week.
Seven starters scored double-digit points. Nobody scored fewer than six.
Aaron Jones gave me 14.8. Alvin Kamara gave me 20.3.
I traded Christian McCaffrey and Derrick Henry because the roster needed to get younger, then won my second game of the year because Aaron Jones and Alvin Kamara combined for 35.1.
Please stop asking me to explain the plan.
Even Marv got me 7.7, and the damage he has done to my brain is now severe enough that I looked at that number and went, "Alright. We'll take it."
Delco is 2-2 now. After opening the year with 128.58, 124.46 and 119.06, this was the first week where the lineup looked remotely like the team I kept insisting was still alive.
Unfortunately, I am also the person who writes these rankings.
So now I have to decide what to do with a 2-2 Delco team immediately after it dropped 157.20.
Move myself up and this entire operation becomes North Korean state media.
Leave myself down and I'm doing that annoying thing where somebody tries so hard to look unbiased that they become even more biased.
I guess I am taking the latter route.
Also, Lamar hurt his ankle.
There we go.
I knew this section was getting a little too positive.
2: Joe has now played four games and scored 15.0, 28.3, 52.5, and 43.12.
Last week I projected 105.
We had a good run, boys.
Somehow, 43.12 was still Joe’s second-highest score of the season.

Tyson Bagent gave him 7.82 of those points in one of the stranger quarterback starts you’ll ever see. Ben Johnson was annoyed that Bagent had been leaked as the starter, so he sent Case Keenum out for the opening snap with Bagent lined up at receiver. He later called it a “ceremonial first pitch.”
Keenum handed the ball off. Ceremony complete. Bagent took over.
Chicago proceeded to run 89 offensive plays while the Jets ran 32. Bagent had an entire afternoon with the football and still managed to become part of Jets history for the wrong reason.
New York entered the game having gone 636 consecutive opponent pass attempts without an interception. An entire 2025 season. Three more games in 2026. Nothing.
Bagent tried his absolute hardest to end it.
He threw four interceptions against the Jets. Three were erased by penalties. The fourth finally counted.
The Jets went an entire season without intercepting anybody, and Joe’s quarterback showed up with enough attempts to make sure one survived review.
Elsewhere, after weeks of us yelling about Tanish collecting running backs while desperately needing receivers, he finally moved one. Kimani Vidal ended up with Joe.
Vidal scored 10.6.
On Joe’s bench.
Tanish then beat him by 117.34.
Beautiful.
And then there’s Jeremiah Smith.
Against Iowa, Smith caught 11 passes for 206 yards and two touchdowns. In PDL scoring, that was 38.1 points.
Connecticut Crocs: 43.12.
Jeremiah Smith: 38.1.
Five points separated the best receiver in the 2027 class from Joe’s entire NFL team.
Smith now has 823 receiving yards and nine touchdowns through five games, which brings us back to the only number Joe should actually care about.
Eight.
Joe owns eight first-round picks in 2027.

So every time Connecticut puts up another score that looks like somebody forgot to set half the lineup, remember that Joe has built himself eight different shots at the class we have been talking about for years. Smith is doing everything possible to make 1.01 the most valuable asset in the league.
3: Alright, Mike. Move over.
The rankings finally caught up to Jeff.
Wichita is 4-0, averaging 164.5 points per week, has already hit 188.4, and just put up 152.42 in the closest thing Jeff has had to a stressful Sunday all season.
There isn't really an argument left.
The funny part is that the NFL version of Jeff's team is currently happening in Kansas City.
The Chiefs are 4-0.
They have Patrick Mahomes.
They have Kenneth Walker.
Their receiver room is getting thin enough that Tyreek Hill rumors have already started.
Jeff is 4-0.
He has Patrick Mahomes.
He has Kenneth Walker.
A.J. Brown is on IR, and Darren spent part of the podcast trying to convince Jeff to turn his 2028 first into Nico Collins.
Apparently once you acquire Mahomes and Walker, the organizational philosophy just downloads automatically.
I'm mostly interested in what Jeff does next, because we're past the point where he needs to prove the roster works.
It works.

He spent the offseason turning draft capital into Joe Burrow, James Cook, Saquon Barkley, Davante Adams, Aaron Rodgers, A.J. Brown, Mark Andrews, Zay Flowers, Jakobi Meyers, Deebo Samuel and Kenneth Walker.
That sentence reads less like a transaction log and more like somebody accidentally turned force trades on.
And after all of that spending, the annoying part is that Darren may be right.
Jeff might need to spend again.
Not because Wichita is in trouble. The opposite.

Kansas City didn't watch Kenneth Walker rip off 177 yards against Vegas, improve to 4-0 and decide the roster was finished. They're looking around because Thornton got hurt, Rice is banged up, and teams that actually believe they're winning the Super Bowl don't usually get sentimental about unused ammunition.
Jeff is staring at roughly the same decision.
A.J. Brown hasn't been available.
Saquon has barely mattered.
The roster has already absorbed enough damage that we were supposed to find out whether this entire win-now experiment had a shelf life.
Instead Jeff is 4-0.
He just beat Greg with 152.
Kenneth Walker is RB2.
Zay Flowers is WR9.
And Patrick Mahomes is on bye this week, so Wichita's emergency plan at quarterback is apparently Joe Burrow and Aaron Rodgers.
Burrow just threw for 428 yards.
Rodgers scored 26 fantasy points.
Very brave of Jeff to weather the Mahomes bye.
That is what separates Wichita from where I had them in the preseason.
I knew the ceiling was stupid. Everyone did. You don't make that many veteran acquisitions without creating something capable of flattening a week.
I wasn't convinced it would hold together.
Four weeks in, the parts that were supposed to make this fragile are barely affecting the results.
Jeff has scored at least 152 in three of four weeks.
He is the highest-scoring team in the league.
He's undefeated.
Mike has spent the first month getting yelled at because I kept Southern Oregon at No. 1.
He can stop yelling now.
Jeff's problem is worse.
Now he has to stay here.
4: Max spent September explaining that Murphy Street was retooling.
Then Darren showed up and apparently the retool came with a Super Bowl.
Max won 143.24 to 130.00, posted the meme, and once Darren was finished, he deliberately left the tight end spot empty.
Kyle Pitts had 7.7 on the bench.
The PDL’s sixth seed is decided by points for.
Max knew that.
But he wanted to send a message.
We finally asked on the podcast whether Darren has quietly replaced Delco as Max’s real rival. Max had already submitted his answer.
Back-to-back championships will move you up the enemies list.
By Tuesday, Darren was explaining Romeo Doubs again.
Darren thinks Doubs sucks. He has been very clear about this.
Doubs scored twice on him.
Darren said the first touchdown happened and he immediately thought:
“Fuck, I’m going to lose.”
Correct.
Then he had to spend part of the podcast explaining why Romeo Doubs still isn’t actually good.
Max gets that audio forever.
Bryce Young came up next.
Darren has never been a Bryce guy either. This week he finally admitted Bryce looks different and might have turned a corner.
Bryce was in Max’s lineup.
Another clip for the folder.
Carnell Tate had the best game of his young career too.
So in the span of one afternoon Max beat Darren and collected fresh evidence for Doubs, Bryce and Tate.
His Notes app is gonna require him to upgrade the cloud storage.
The funniest part of the “Super Bowl” thing is that Max did not just say it afterward.
He actually behaved like the season ended.
Game over.
Pitts out.
Points no longer necessary.
See everybody at Disney World.
Max can resume the retool whenever he gets back.
He is 2-2.
More importantly, he is 1-0 this year against his rival.
There is one thing looming in my mind, though, while Max continues his celebration.
What if Murphy Street goes on a Cinderella run but misses the sixth seed by 7.7 points or fewer in December?
Imagine the chaos.
5: Jon lost by 87 and somehow came out of the week with an anonymous mailbag asking us to congratulate him.
Kenyon Sadiq is third among rookies in scoring.
Antonio Williams is fifth.
Malachi Fields is seventh.

Darren’s first response on the podcast:
“Did Jon write this himself?”
We’re a month from the midterms and Richmond is already facing allegations of ballot stuffing.
Sadiq followed last week’s 7-catch, 105-yard touchdown game with a zero.
The Jets ran 32 offensive plays.
Chicago ran 89.
Fernando Mendoza is still waiting behind Kirk Cousins, who has chosen age 38 to rediscover mobility.
365 yards. Two touchdowns. Vegas is 3-1.
Taylor Swift-Kelce made a surprise SNL appearance Saturday night and still got on television before Mendoza did.
Makai Lemon at least got the opportunity Jon has been waiting for.
DeVonta Smith out.
Hollywood Brown out.
Three catches for 27 yards.
Darius Cooper still played more and scored twice.
Jon is going to know Philadelphia’s receiver rotation with the intimacy of a position coach by Thanksgiving.
Mike Washington followed last week’s touchdown with nine carries for 18 yards and one catch for minus-one.
Earlier this year Lemon opened with three catches for minus-five.
Richmond’s rookie class has a strange fascination with the other side of the line of scrimmage.
Then Tyquan Thornton finally gave Jon a real explosion.

Five catches.
111 yards.
Two touchdowns.
25.6 points.
On the bench.
Then he dislocated his ankle on a 55-yard catch.
Sleeper fit the entire Richmond experience into one row.
Jon probably spent less time looking at the 60.82 than he did checking Sadiq’s routes, Lemon’s snap share and Thornton’s MRI timeline.
Which is probably correct.
He did not build this thing for October 2026.
He built it so that, eventually, one of these Saturdays and Sundays stops feeling like homework.
Right now the rebuild is at least starting to hand back graded assignments.
And apparently Jon got three A’s.
6: Last week the mailbag wanted Brian to trade his 2028 first and make a run.
Nico Collins came back, went 7 for 118 and two touchdowns, and apparently convinced everyone to start shopping him instead.
By Tuesday, the podcast had already found buyers.
Tanish.
Jeff.
Basically anybody near the top of the standings with a first-round pick and functioning ambition.
Brian has now issued his response:
“Nico will remain a valued member of the Hu$tle unless I get an offer I can’t refuse.”
So there it is.
The league has placed Nico on the trade block.
Brian has not.
Nico is 27, which makes him ancient compared to half of Hollywood’s roster, but he also just came back from injury and immediately looked like Nico Collins again.
That is a difficult player to casually ship out because everyone else has decided your timeline for you.
Darren wants Nico sold.
Kirk Cousins should apparently go too.
Pat Freiermuth can pack a bag.
At this rate Brian is going to log into Sleeper and find his roster staged for an open house.
The timing on Cousins is pretty good too.
He gave Hollywood 25.6 while Raiders coach Klint Kubiak told CBS at halftime:
“We’re gonna win the game.”
Kansas City won 30-27.
Brian is 1-3.
Keep that clip handy.
Hollywood’s problem is that there is enough here to talk yourself into almost anything.
Nico is still Nico.
Jeremiyah Love, Egbuka and Tuten are young enough to wait on.
Kirk is suddenly useful.
Then Brett beats him anyway because Tetairoa McMillan decides their rival-podcast matchup is the proper setting for 38.2 points.
Brian now gets to record with the guy who just helped put him at 1-3.
Darren also picked Hollywood to make the playoffs before the season.
That prediction got dragged back onto the podcast this week alongside his other rapidly aging takes.
The Chargers are fine.
Brian makes the playoffs.
Deshaun Watson won’t keep this up.
Watson should probably start preparing the MVP speech now.
The Nico question is going to sit over Hollywood until something changes.
Brian just said he is keeping him unless somebody comes with an offer he cannot refuse.
Which means every contender in the PDL just read that sentence and immediately opened the trade calculator.
As the completely neutral owner of Brian’s 2027 first, I never really understood why he went to this roster to begin with.
Nico deserves a fantasy team where he doesn't have to do everything himself like on his real-life team.
Will we see Nico move? Doubtful, but this is McFatty we are talking about.
7: Max called this his Super Bowl.
I think he undersold the audience.

There were probably people happier about Murphy Street beating Darren 143.24-130.00 than they were about their own matchup. Darren has reached that very specific level of PDL villain where nobody needs Max to be good. They just needed him to be good for one Sunday.
And Max delivered.
The timing was especially brutal because Darren was already having a rough week in the court of public opinion.
Two weeks ago he said he wasn't buying that the Chargers were actually bad.
They immediately played two horrendous games.
His preseason hot take was Hollywood making the playoffs.
Brian is 1-3.
Now Darren says he isn't buying the Deshaun Watson comeback.
At this point Cleveland should probably hear that and start clearing cap space for another fully guaranteed contract.
Watson has outscored one of Darren's starting quarterbacks every week. Darren admitted that himself.
He still won't start him.
This week Stafford gave him 7.7. Watson had 13.9 sitting on the bench.
For a man who has spent years fighting allegations that he only talks about his own team on the podcast, he is showing remarkable restraint when it comes to believing in one of his own players.
Unfortunately, this is about where the fun ends.
Because you open the rest of the roster and remember why everybody wanted Max to win so badly.
Jahmyr Gibbs is RB1.
CeeDee Lamb is WR2.
Brock Bowers and George Kittle are both in the starting lineup.
T.J. Hockenson scored 24.9 last week.
On Darren's bench.
Most teams get 24.9 from a tight end and spend Tuesday talking about how they finally solved the position.
Darren got 24.9 and basically had nowhere to put it.
That's really the problem with Philadelphia.
Even the loss is irritating.
You want the Max upset to expose something. You want to open the roster afterward and find the loose thread. Something that makes you think maybe the Thunder aren't quite what we thought.
Instead, you find Garrett Wilson having a slow start and a quarterback room where Darren keeps benching the guy currently making him look stupid.
That's about it.
So Max gets his Super Bowl.
Darren loses the undefeated season.
And I still have to put Philadelphia third.
Trust me, I know how unsatisfying that is.
8: An NFL official got suspended for two games this week after cursing at Trey McBride.
I beat McBride's fantasy owner by 40 points and then ranked him two spots above me.
Apparently I am the only official in football overcorrecting.
157.20 to 116.48. Same 2-2 record. Head-to-head advantage. Welch stays above Delco.
I never want to hear about bias again.
Green Bay spent Sunday leaning into 13 personnel against Tampa. Welch has apparently been installing the same offense in Dallas for a month.

Trey McBride.
Juwan Johnson.
Harold Fannin.
All three start.
McBride is TE1. Juwan is TE3. Fannin is TE7.
Normally starting three tight ends in fantasy means something has gone terribly wrong. Welch is doing it on purpose and with intent.
Christian Watson is WR6 too, so at this point Matt LaFleur could probably borrow Welch's Sleeper login and finish his game plan.
The problem is what happened behind them.
Bucky Irving and David Montgomery combined for 10.4 points against me.
Kyren Williams scored 31.7 by himself.
I don't bring that up to gloat.
I bring it up to gloat, and because Derrick Henry went on the trade block about 48 hours later.
Darren immediately named Welch as one of the teams that should be calling Greg, and I hate how cleanly that fits.
Welch does not need another quarterback. Dak and Goff are fine.
He doesn't need another receiver.
For the love of God, he does not need another tight end.
He needs exactly the type of running back Greg has suddenly decided he may no longer need.
The timing is especially funny because Baltimore just lost Lamar Jackson to an ankle injury, which should make Derrick Henry more important to the Ravens.
London lost one fantasy matchup and decided to see what the market looks like.
Same Derrick Henry. Very different emergency meeting.

And Welch has already shown us what he does when he sees a problem. He doesn't sit around waiting for it to fix itself. He went and got Dak after the quarterback room started getting weird. Dallas has been one of the more aggressive teams in the league whenever Welch thinks the roster is close enough to justify it.
This roster is close enough.
That's why the 116.48 doesn't bother me much.
The loss actually made the next move easier to see.

If Welch turns around after getting his ass kicked by Delco and comes out of it with Derrick Henry, then I will have spent Sunday beating Dallas by 40 points only to help Welch diagnose the one part of his roster that needed fixing.
Excellent.
I love contributing to other people's championship runs.
9: I need Greg to stop making me look stupid.
Before the season, I picked London to win the league as my hot take. Four weeks later, Greg appears to be treating that prediction as a personal insult.
This was supposed to be the payoff.

He spent years tearing the roster down, hoarding assets, building probably the deepest running back room in the league, and generally behaving like a man who enjoyed the offseason more than the actual sport. Then the rebuild finally worked. Bijan. Derrick Henry. Quinshon Judkins. Herbert. Nix. Higgins. Olave.
A real contender.
Apparently that was the problem.
Greg spent roughly two years and 46 trade offers trying to get Rome Odunze. He finally did it, sending Chris Olave away to Mike in the process.
Four games later, Derrick Henry is on the trade block.
I think we may have misunderstood Greg this entire time.
He doesn't want to finish a rebuild.
He wants to rebuild.
Because what exactly happened this week that triggered the evacuation order?
London scored 140.02 points.
They lost to Jeff, who is 4-0 and currently bulldozing his way through the league like Kenneth Walker apparently bulldozes the final five minutes of a Raiders game.
That's it.

This wasn't Joe scoring 43 points. Nobody found Greg wandering around the waiver wire looking for a second starting quarterback. Bijan gave him 27.2. Tee Higgins gave him 21.2. Quinshon gave him 18.6.
Even Rome had his best receiving game of the season, catching six balls for 94 yards.
Greg finally got Rome.
Rome finally started looking like the guy Greg spent 46 offers trying to acquire.
And Greg responded by putting Derrick Henry on Facebook Marketplace.
The Bears have now survived an early season that included Case Keenum and Tyson Bagent playing quarterback and somehow came out of it 3-1.
Greg lost one fantasy matchup while scoring 140 and has begun liquidating the estate.
I thought Mike was the one who tilts/panics?

The funniest part is that Henry isn't even some dead roster weight he has been dragging around; he's averaging 21.8 points through four weeks. Greg is looking at one of the best running backs on his team, on a team that is 2-2, four games into the season, and going, "You know what? Perhaps somebody else should have this."
They're 2-2.
They just scored 140.

Bijan looks ridiculous. Quinshon is producing. Higgins is healthy enough to matter. Rome is finally showing signs of life. Bo Nix exists. Justin Herbert also technically exists, although Greg benching him for Geno Smith last week may have been the most devastating Herbert analysis anyone has produced all season.
This team does not need a rebuild.
I think some people are simply built for it. Give Greg eight future picks, a roster projected for 83 points and three years of runway, and he's completely at peace.
Give him an actual contender with expectations and by Week 4 he's standing outside the stadium with a FOR SALE sign.
Maybe this is how London operates forever.
Build contender.
Become terrified of contender.
Sell contender.
Build better contender.
Repeat until 2034.
At some point, Greg is going to have to suffer through the indignity of actually playing a full regular season.
Preferably this one.
I already picked him to win the league.
10: Indiana beat Rutgers 47-15 this weekend.
They improved to 5-0.
The AP voters dropped them from No. 6 to No. 7.
Mike, I finally found precedent.
Southern Oregon beat Richmond 147.54 to 60.82, improved to 4-0, and has been removed from the top spot in the PDL Power Rankings.
I want it entered into the record that I did not cave to three straight weeks of complaints.
The AP Poll simply gave me legal cover.
Mike scored 147 points in a week where Josh Allen was...fine.
19.5 points.
QB13.
For literally anyone else, that is a normal Josh Allen game. In Southern Oregon, it qualifies as the franchise quarterback taking PTO.
Brock Purdy covered for him with 23.6.
Which is timely, because apparently Mina Kimes and a 49ers reporter spent part of this week arguing online about whether Purdy was actually good against Denver.
Mike can stay out of it.
Sleeper currently has Purdy as QB1.
Josh Allen is QB2.
There are entire franchises in this league currently trying to establish whether they own one reliable quarterback, and Mike has accidentally cornered the market on the position.
It also makes his Justin Herbert victory lap significantly more annoying.
Mike spent part of this week demanding an apology because he left Herbert outside his preseason top 12 and everyone thought he was being an Oregon contrarian.
Four weeks later, Herbert is QB25.
Mike has QB1 and QB2.
I would like to formally apologize for doubting Mike.
The rest of the roster isn't giving us much help either.
Achane is on IR.
Charbonnet still hasn't played.
Mike responded by trading for Ollie Gordon and Jalen Wright, and Gordon immediately gave him 17 points.
Puka was back over 20.
LaPorta was back over 20.

Olave, who Mike acquired while Greg was busy completing his lifelong quest for Rome Odunze, is WR4.
This is becoming less of a fantasy roster and more of evidence in Greg's eventual competency hearing.

And yet, after all of that:
No. 2.
So Southern Oregon gets the Indiana treatment.
Win convincingly.
Remain undefeated.
Drop anyway.
You all spent three weeks yelling at me about this.
Smoke is finally No. 2.
Please find something else to be mad about.
11: Paramount and Warner Bros officially became one company this week.
Brett and Brian went the other direction.
The rival podcast co-hosts finally got their head-to-head, and Dubrovnik took it 123.48 to 114.08 for its first win. (I love you, Brett. Signed: Someone with Brian's 2027 1st)
Tetairoa McMillan spent Sunday night making sure Brian would have something to talk about on the next episode.

At halftime:
9 catches. 147 yards. Touchdown.
Brian still had another half to watch.

Final:
14 catches. 192 yards. Two touchdowns. 38.2 points.
Last week Tet had two catches for 17 yards.
Rebuilds are more fun when the good players start doing this.
Brett has never really pretended 2026 was supposed to be the year. He wanted Dart, Hampton, Tet, Loveland, Boston, and the rest of the young group to start giving him something tangible.
Tet just did it on Sunday Night Football.

Then the anonymous mailbag arrived Tuesday with an extremely important announcement:
Denzel Boston is currently the highest-scoring rookie through four weeks.
Darren immediately asked whether Brett submitted it himself.
I’m picturing Brett dismissing his class for lunch and sprinting to the mailbag form.
Boston is on Dubrovnik, of course.
Colston Loveland also entered Sunday with one catch for three yards on the entire season.
Six catches for 57 this week.
He exists.
Brett even left Brian Robinson’s 25.2 on the bench.
Three touchdowns.
Didn’t need them.
There was a stretch over the first few weeks where nearly every interesting young player Brett owned was either hurt, invisible or both.
This week Tet went insane, Loveland finally caught footballs, Boston continued building his anonymous-mailbag résumé, and Brett got his first win.
Against Brian.
It has been a while since we got an episode of the Disrespected so maybe we need to start ruffling some more feathers.
12: Terry Bradshaw spent Sunday morning suggesting the Patriots might need to bench Drake Maye.
Tanish spent the week trading for Jameis Winston.
By Sunday night, Maye had thrown three touchdowns, New England had handed Buffalo its first loss of the season, and Boulder had 31.2 points from the quarterback position.
Really strong week for the Drake Maye confidence committee.
The Winston trade made some sense when it happened.
Caleb was hurt. Jayden was hurt. Maye had just scored 1.76. Tanish had spent years collecting quarterbacks and somehow reached the one week where he might actually need another one.
So he sent Kimani Vidal and a fourth for Winston and Seth McGowan.
Then he drew Joe.
Jameis could have stayed wherever he was.
The better part of the trade is McGowan, because it gets us back to my favorite ongoing Boulder mystery.
What exactly does Tanish think his roster needs?
Kansas City watched Rashee Rice pull up with a hamstring injury Sunday and immediately started sniffing around a Tyreek Hill reunion.
Tanish watched Rashee Rice pull up with a hamstring injury and had just used trade capital to acquire Jonathan Taylor's backup.
This is why Darren and I sound insane every time we talk about Boulder.
Tanish's WR3 right now is Mack Hollins.
Mack Hollins is now questionable.
Travis Hunter gave him 0.0 last week and has spent most of his time playing defense.
Rashee Rice is hurt.
The defending champion has JSN, Nabers, and then a depth chart that starts getting uncomfortable very quickly.

Meanwhile:
Jonathan Taylor.
Chase Brown.
Jaylen Warren.
Rhamondre Stevenson.
Chuba Hubbard.
Seth McGowan.
Najee Harris.
Justice Hill.
Samaje Perine.
Tyrone Tracy.
Ty Johnson.
Tanish finally traded one running back away and still had Chuba score 25.4 points on his bench.
He has accomplished subtraction without reducing the total.
And somehow none of it mattered because Boulder scored 160.46, the highest total in the league.
I have been waiting for this roster construction to punish Tanish since sometime during his championship run last year.
Instead, every time I point at something and say, "See, this is finally going to matter," Boulder wins another game.
Too many quarterbacks?
Maye walks into Buffalo and beats the undefeated Bills.
Too many running backs?
Chuba drops 25 on the bench.
Not enough receivers?
JSN is currently WR1.
Tanish is 3-1.
At some point I have to consider the possibility that the roster isn't poorly constructed and I just don't understand whatever he's building.
Still.
Go trade for a receiver.
Andy Reid figured this out in about three hours.
